chunks: That which the Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me of; he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed me, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yasin al-Basri, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him):

that he was asked about stagnant water in which animals urinate. He said: "If the water changes (in quality), do not perform wudu from it; and if their urine does not change it, then perform wudu from it. And likewise blood, when it flows into water, and similar things."

key_terms.أَبْوَالُهَا: their urine — the najis substance entering the water
key_terms.اَلدَّوَابُّ: animals/beasts of burden — four-legged working animals
key_terms.اَلْمَاءِ اَلنَّقِيعِ: stagnant/pooled water — still, collected water as opposed to flowing water
key_terms.تَغَيَّرَ: to change (in properties) — the decisive criterion for water becoming ritually impure

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) on performing wudu from stagnant water in which animals have urinated?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was asked about stagnant water in which animals urinate, and he ruled that if the water's properties (color, smell, or taste) are altered it may not be used for wudu, but if unchanged it remains valid. The same criterion — change of properties — applies equally to blood and similar impurities entering water, establishing a single jurisprudential standard for water's ritual purity.
